{"content":[{"fragments":[{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/0","text":"Computer Science > Computation and Language"},{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/1","text":"[Submitted on 6 Oct 2022 (v1), last revised 10 Mar 2023 (this version, v3)]"},{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/2","text":"Title:ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models"},{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/3","text":"Authors:Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao"},{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/4","text":"View a PDF of the paper titled ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models, by Shunyu Yao and 6 other authors"},{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/5","text":"View PDF HTML (experimental)"},{"kind":"text","location":"#/texts/6","text":"Abstract:While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities across tasks in language understanding and interactive decision making, their abilities for reasoning (e.g. chain-of-thought prompting) and acting (e.g. action plan generation) have primarily been studied as separate topics. In this paper, we explore the use of LLMs to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, allowing for greater synergy between the two: reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans as well as handle exceptions, while actions allow it to interface with external sources, such as knowledge bases or environments, to gather additional information. We apply our approach, named ReAct, to a diverse set of language and decision making tasks and demonstrate its effectiveness over state-of-the-art baselines, as well as improved human interpretability and trustworthiness over methods without reasoning or acting components. Concretely, on question answering (HotpotQA) and fact verification (Fever), ReAct overcomes issues of hallucination and error propagation prevalent in chain-of-thought reasoning by interacting with a simple Wikipedia API, and generates human-like task-solving trajectories that are more interpretable than baselines without reasoning traces. On two interactive decision making benchmarks (ALFWorld and WebShop), ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by an absolute success rate of 34% and 10% respectively, while being prompted with only one or two in-context examples. citations.quote: Abstract:While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities across tasks in language understanding and interactive decision making, their abilities for reasoning (e.g. chain-of-thought prompting) and acting (e.g. action plan generation) have primarily been studied as separate topics. In this paper, we explore the use of LLMs to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, allowing for greater synergy between the two: reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans as well as handle exceptions, while actions allow it to interface with external sources, such as knowledge bases or environments, to gather additional information.
citations.reasoning: 该摘要片段说明 ReAct 以交错方式生成推理轨迹与任务特定动作，并说明动作可与外部知识库或环境交互以获取信息，但未提供逐轮轨迹，证明此页仅为摘要层级的机制概述。

claims.statement: 用户提供的 arXiv abs 页（arXiv:2210.03629）仅为摘要页而非全文；search_source 定位到的机制描述位于摘要片段 #/texts/6，未包含论文正文中的 thought/action/observation 逐轮轨迹。

citations.quote: ReAct enables language models to generate both verbal reasoning traces and text actions in an interleaved manner. While actions lead to observation feedback from an external environment (“Env” in the figure below), reasoning traces do not affect the external environment. Instead, they affect the internal state of the model by reasoning over the context and updating it with useful information to support future reasoning and acting.
citations.reasoning: 这是官方的机制性陈述，直接对应 thought（推理轨迹）、action（动作）、observation（观察反馈）的交替关系，可作为一级资料引用。该来源为 Google Research Blog，由论文作者 Shunyu Yao 与 Yuan Cao 署名发布。

claims.statement: Google Research Blog 官方博客《ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models》（2022-11-08）已获取全文，并明确描述 ReAct 机制：模型以交错方式生成言语推理轨迹与文本动作；动作导致来自外部环境的观察反馈，推理痕迹不影响外部环境，而是通过上下文推理更新模型内部状态以支持后续推理与行动。

citations.quote: Use the human-in-the-loop (HITL) flow to pause agent execution until a person approves or rejects sensitive tool calls.
citations.reasoning: 这是官方一级工程文档，直接描述了人工批准/拒绝工具调用前暂停执行的流程，符合“先计划-人工确认-再执行”的来源要求。

claims.statement: OpenAI Agents SDK 官方文档《Human-in-the-loop》已获取全文，明确说明 HITL 流程会暂停 agent 执行，直到人工批准或拒绝敏感工具调用。

missing: OpenReview PDF 全文因重定向或 URL 变化而获取失败，未能核对论文正文中的逐轮轨迹细节。
claims.statement: OpenReview 上的 ReAct ICLR 版全文 PDF（https://openreview.net/pdf?id=WE_vluYUL-X）未能获取，因 fetch_web 返回“Fetched source redirected or changed URL”，因此无法从论文正文直接提供逐轮 thought/action/observation 轨迹的全文级摘录。

output.report: 已完成 ReAct 原论文机制证据核对与官方“先规划-人工确认-再执行”来源检索，锁定 3 份可引用的一级资料。第 1 份为用户提供的 arXiv abs 页（2210.03629），经 search_source 定位确认其仅为摘要页而非全文，无 thought/action/observation 交替机制的逐轮细节。第 2 份为 Google Research Blog 官方博客《ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models》（2022-11-08），已获取全文，明确描述 ReAct 以交错方式生成言语推理轨迹与文本动作，动作触发外部环境观察反馈，推理痕迹更新模型内部状态以支持后续推理与行动；该博客确认机制核心，但未展示论文正文中的逐轮轨迹表格。第 3 份为 OpenAI Agents SDK 官方文档《Human-in-the-loop》，已获取全文，明确说明 HITL 流程会暂停 agent 执行，直到人工批准或拒绝敏感工具调用。OpenReview 的论文全文 PDF（openreview.net/pdf?id=WE_vluYUL-X）在 fetch 时因重定向或 URL 变化而不可用，未能取得 ICLR 版全文正文。
missing: ReAct 论文 ICLR 版全文正文未获取：OpenReview PDF（https://openreview.net/pdf?id=WE_vluYUL-X）在 fetch_web 时返回“Fetched source redirected or changed URL”，因此无法从论文正文直接核对 thought/action/observation 逐轮交替的完整轨迹细节。当前机制证据来自 arXiv 摘要页与 Google Research Blog 官方博客的一级说明。
arXiv abs 页（2210.03629）仅为摘要页而非全文，无法作为逐轮机制细节的全文级证据。
